messages.subject: using discrete latent in model
parts:
Dear All,

I have a model that include a discrete latent and right censored data (the attached pdf file). If I could use discrete variable in parameters block (I know I can not), I think my model was as follows:

data
        {
        int<lower=0> n;
        real S[n];
        int<lower=0,upper=1> D[n];
        real d;
        }
       
parameters
        {
        real<lower=0, upper=1> p;
        real mu0;
        real mu1;
        real<lower=0> sigma0;
        real<lower=0> sigma1;
        int<lower=0,upper=1> Z[n];
        }
   
model
        {
        real su;
        su = 0;
       
        p ~ uniform(0, 1)
        mu0 ~ normal(20, 10);
        mu1 ~ normal(25, 10);
        sigma0 ~ uniform(0.01, 0.5);
        sigma1 ~ uniform(0.01, 0.5);
       
        Z ~ bernoulli(p)
       
        for(i in 1:n) su = su + D[i] * ( (1-Z[i])*normal_lpdf(S[i]|mu0,sigma0) + Z[i]*normal_lpdf(S[i]|mu1,sigma1) )
                              + (1-D[i]) * ( (1-Z[i])*normal_lcdf(mu0|d,sigma0) + Z[i]* normal_lcdf(mu1|d,sigma1) ) ;
        target += su;
        }


Is there a way to define this model in Stan?

Best,

- Bistoon

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] using discrete latent in model
parts:
D[i] (censored or not) and Z[i] (mixture component) are
both boolean, you can much more efficiently write

>
> su = 0;

> for(i in 1:n) su = su + D[i] * ( (1-Z[i])*normal_lpdf(S[i]|mu0,sigma0) + Z[i]*normal_lpdf(S[i]|mu1,sigma1) )
> + (1-D[i]) * ( (1-Z[i])*normal_lcdf(mu0|d,sigma0) + Z[i]* normal_lcdf(mu1|d,sigma1) ) ;
> target += su;

by converting those mu and sigma to vectors of size 2 and writing
the following, which I think gets the truncation in the more
traditional order and uses

for (i in 1:n)
if (D[i]) {
target += normal_lpdf(S[i] | mu[1 + Z[i]], sigma[1 + Z[i]]);
} else {
target += normal_lcdf(LB | mu[1 + Z[i]], sigma[1 + Z[i]]);
}

That gives you a truncation point trunc, such that if D[0] = 1,
all you know is that the value is less than LB (that is, values
below LB are truncated). If you want the truncation to go the
other way, you need to use the lccdf. There's a long discussion
in the manual of all this.

Now you have things in a form where you can deal with the fact
that really

Z[i] ~ bernoulli(p);

So what you do is this:

if (D[i])
target += log_mix(p, normal_lpdf(S[i] | mu[1], sigma[1]),
normal_lpdf(S[i] | mu[2], sigma[2]));
else
... same deal ...

- Bob
